claims: The Artemis II mission is a crewed mission.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch from NASA's Kennedy Space Center.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch at 6:24 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II mission aims for a ~10-day trip around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission will travel roughly 252,799 miles from Earth.
The Artemis II mission splashdown is planned in the Pacific Ocean.
The Artemis II mission splashdown is planned for April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II launch site is Kennedy Space Center, Launch Complex 39B.
The Artemis II mission duration is ~10 days.
The Artemis II mission includes an initial orbit of ~24 hours checking systems in Earth orbit.
The Artemis II trans-lunar injection is scheduled to send the crew towards the Moon.
The Artemis II lunar flyby follows an approx. four-day journey to the Moon.
The Artemis II launch window is 5:24–7:24 pm CT (6:24–8:24 pm ET).
Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 2 at 6:22 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 3 at 7:00 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 4 at 7:53 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 5 at 8:40 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 6 at 9:36 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
Backup launch opportunities for the Artemis II mission are available on April 30 at 5:06 pm CDT if the April 1 launch is delayed.
Artemis II mission Day 1 includes launch to Earth orbit and initial checkouts.
Artemis II mission Days 2-3 include trans-lunar injection, safety checks, and system tests.
Artemis II mission Day 4 includes lunar flyby, lunar imaging, and trajectory adjustments.
Artemis II mission Day 7 includes journey back to Earth, leaving the lunar sphere of influence.
Artemis II mission Days 8-9 include radiation protection tests and manual steering tests.
Artemis II mission Day 10 includes re-entry, parachute deployment, and splashdown.
Reid Wiseman is the Commander of the Artemis II crew.
Victor Glover is the Pilot of the Artemis II crew.
Christina Koch is a Mission Specialist on the Artemis II crew.
Jeremy Hansen is a Mission Specialist on the Artemis II crew.
